claim.claim-text: 1. An ultrasonic flow meter comprising at least one ultrasonic transducer (TR1, TR2) and a signal generator (SG) for generating electrical signals to the transducer (TR1, TR2), the signal generator (SG) comprising an active component (OPsg), characterized in that the flow meter further includes means for measuring one or more power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) to the active component (OPsg) of the signal generator (SG).

2. The flow meter according to claim 1, wherein the means for measuring one or more power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) comprise a resistor (R8; RCC) inserted in series between the source of the positive supply voltage (V3; VCC) and the active component (OPsg) and/or a resistor (R43) inserted in series between the source of the negative supply voltage and the active component (OPsg).
3. The flow meter according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the means for measuring one or more power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) comprise a receiver circuit (RC) of said flow meter.

4. The flow meter according to any one of the previous claims, arranged to feed a pulsating input signal (DPSa, DPSb) or a single pulse input signal (SP) to said signal generator (SG) to generate said electrical signal to the transducer (TR1, TR2).

5. The flow meter according to any one of the previous claims, arranged to determine directly from the obtained one or more power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) or from one or more resulting signals (SCS-, SCS+; SPSCS0) derived from the one or more obtained power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) one or more quantities useful for characterizing the transducer (TR1, TR2).

6. The flow meter according to claim 5, wherein the quantities useful for characterizing the transducer (TR1, TR2) include an oscillation period (Tscs) and/or a damping coefficient (α) determined from at least a part of one or more of the obtained power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) and/or the derived signals (SCS-, SCS+; SPSCS0), said signal part representing a dampened oscillation.

7. The flow meter according to any one of the previous claims, comprising two of said ultrasonic transducers (TR1, TR2), and being arranged to measure the at least one power supply current (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) for each of the two ultrasonic transducers (TR1, TR2).

8. The flow meter according to claim 7, wherein the flow meter is a transit time based ultrasonic flow meter arranged to determine the absolute transit time (t<d>) of an ultrasonic signal in a flow path (FP) of said flow meter on the basis of said measured power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) for each of the two ultrasonic transducers (TR1, TR2).

9. Method of measuring one or more power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) to an active component (OPsg) of a signal generator (SG) of an ultrasonic flow meter, the signal generator (SG) generating electrical signals to an ultrasonic transducer (TR1, TR2), the method comprising:

feeding a pulsating input signal (DPSa, DPSb) or a single pulse input signal (SP) to the signal generator (SG), monitoring the current to the active component (OPsg) from one or more voltage supplies (VCC; V3) during and after the feeding of the input signal (DPSa, DPSb; SP) to the signal generator (SG), thus obtaining one or more supply current signal (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2).
10. A method for characterizing an ultrasonic transducer (TR1, TR2), said method comprising the steps of:

feeding a pulsating input signal (DPSa, DPSb) or a single pulse input signal (SP) to a signal generator (SG) driving the transducer (TR1, TR2), said signal generator comprising an active component (OPsg), monitoring the current to the active component (OPsg) from one or more voltage supplies (VCC; V3) during and after the feeding of the input signal (DPSa, DPSb) to the signal generator (SG), thus obtaining one or more supply current signal (SCSa, SCSb), and determining directly from the obtained one or more supply current signal (SCSa, SCSb) or from one or more resulting signals (SCS-, SCS+) derived from the one or more obtained supply current signal (SCSa, SCSb) one or more quantities useful for characterizing the transducer (TR1, TR2).

11. The method according to claim 10, wherein the quantities useful for characterizing the transducer (TR1, TR2) include an oscillation period (Tscs) and/or a damping coefficient (α) determined from at least a part of one or more of the obtained signals (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) and/or the derived signals (SCS-, SCS+; SPSCS0), said signal part representing a dampened oscillation.

12. The method according to claim 9 or the method according to claim 10 or 11, wherein the one or more supply current signals (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) are obtained by monitoring the voltage across one or more current sensing resistors (RCC, R8; R43) being arranged in series between the active component (OPsg) of the signal generator (SG) and one or more voltage supplies (VCC, V3) of the signal generator (SG).

13. The method according to claim 9 or the method according to any one of the claims 10 to 12, comprising measuring the at least one power supply current (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) for each of two ultrasonic transducers (TR1, TR2).

14. The method according to claim 13, wherein the flow meter is a transit time based ultrasonic flow meter, and wherein the method comprises determining the absolute transit time (t<d>) of an ultrasonic signal in a flow path (FP) of said flow meter on the basis of said measured power supply currents (SCSa, SCSb; SPSCS1, SPSCS2) for each of the two ultrasonic transducers (TR1, TR2).
15. The method according to claim 9 or the method according to any one of the claims 10 to 14, wherein the flow meter is an ultrasonic flow meter according to any of the claims 1 to 8.
